title: Pilot: sensitive data paths, benchmarking & retention scoping
meeting_header: 2026-09-02 14:00 PDT | 45 minutes | Attendees: Maya, Derrick (Redwood); Priya, Carlos, Janet, Evan (LumenBank)
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week pilot to validate sensitive-data handling and performance. Focus areas: PII detection/redaction, prompt retention options, retention TTLs, benchmark workload sizing (tokens/second, concurrency), and success criteria (p95 latency, accuracy on redaction, throughput). Action: Redwood to propose benchmark plan and SOW; customer to provide redaction examples and sample prompts.
transcript:
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'll kick off — i'm Maya, AE on the account. Derrick's our solutions engineer.
00:12 Priya: Hi Maya, thanks. Priya here. we're trying to scope a pilot to validate how your inference handles our live chat workload and, crucially, how sensitive fields are protected.
00:26 Derrick: great, thanks Priya. can you give us a sense of current numbers — messages per day, average tokens per request, and concurrency? that will shape the benchmark plan.
00:36 Carlos: yeah, so currently about 120k messages/day, avg 180 tokens per user message, peak concurrent sessions around 350 during day. bursts can go to 700 for short windows.
00:49 Janet: and from compliance — we're mandated to retain certain transcripts for 90 days, but customer-identifying fields must be redacted within 24 hours unless flagged. so retention + fast redaction are both requirements.
01:05 Maya: okay that helps. quick note: in Redwood pilots we can run two benchmark phases — a perf baseline (latency/throughput) and a functional redaction accuracy run (compare automated redaction against your ground truth).
01:20 Evan: what's the expected turnaround? we want to show results to stakeholders in three weeks.
01:25 Derrick: technically we can run a 2-week pilot: a few days for onboarding and data prep, 5–7 days perf bench, 3–4 days functional redaction eval, and buffer for analysis. three weeks is tight but feasible if we parallelize prep.
01:39 Priya: what's the model hosting mode you'd recommend? hosted API for speed? or dedicated for predictable latency? cost tradeoffs?
01:47 Derrick: for production-like latency at your concurrency, Dedicated is recommended — reserved GPU pools give predictable p95. but for a pilot we can use hosted with a dedicated-capacity pilot pool or a short-lived dedicated node. costs and SLA differ. I'll include cost scenarios in the SOW.
02:02 Janet: security checklist — SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS for encryption at rest, audit logs. We also need the ability to disable prompt retention or opt-out per-customer. how does Redwood support that?
02:14 Maya: good question. Redwood has per-customer retention profiles and an option to disable persistent prompt storage for specific routes. for pilots we can set retention to 0 for flagged routes and keep ephemeral caching only for latency. there are caveats on debugging because logs will be limited.
02:29 Carlos: is the redaction step performed client-side, at the API gateway, or within Redwood? we prefer redaction before it hits shared logs.
02:37 Derrick: redaction can be done in multiple places. options: pre-send client-side sanitizer (we can provide regex/heuristic templates), server-side pre-processing on a private deployment (VPC) using your redaction library, or Redwood-managed post-hoc redaction on logs. for highest assurance, running the sanitizer in your stack (client or VPC private runtime) is ideal.
02:52 Priya: we will likely want to evaluate both — our compliance team will also sample post-hoc logs to validate. can the platform run differential tests so we can measure false positives/negatives?
03:02 Derrick: yes, we'll run functional tests where we compare automated redaction results against your annotated ground truth dataset. we'll report precision/recall and give examples.
03:11 Maya: on retention TTLs — what are you expecting? you mentioned 24-hour mandatory redaction.
03:16 Janet: ideally metadata and non-identifying content kept 90 days as per business need, but any PII must be redacted or removed from logs within 24 hours. legal may ask for audit trails that show the deletion event.
03:30 Derrick: we can set retention policy and emit deletion events to your audit log; for pilots we can demo that via a webhook or S3 lifecycle artifact. we'll also show KMS-wrapped storage for any persisted artifacts.
03:41 Carlos: about benchmarks — what's the metric list? p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and tail latency under burst?
03:49 Derrick: correct, plus sustained throughput, model warmup behavior (cold vs hot kv cache), and token-per-request distribution. we'll run a 3-tier workload: nominal (average traffic), peak (350 concurrent) and stress (700 short burst).
04:05 Priya: do you simulate user prompt complexity? our prompts include code snippets and multi-turn context, sometimes 2–3k tokens.
04:13 Derrick: we'll include mixed sequence lengths in thebench harness. note that longer context affects latency and memory; we'll capture model variant metrics (e.g., quantized variants) so you can see tradeoffs.
04:26 Evan: what about prompt leakage concerns — storing prompts for debug is risky. we need per-route opt-out and a safe-mode where prompts are never stored.
04:35 Maya: that's doable. Redwood offers per-route retention and a safe-mode flag. in safe-mode, we do not write full prompts to persistent logs; ephemeral caches may still exist for the duration of the request for performance but are not persisted.
04:50 Janet: will we get a paper trail that says prompt payloads were not stored? auditors need proofs.
04:57 Derrick: we can produce an audit artifact — a signed log that indicates retention flags and deletion timestamps; integration with your KMS gives additional attestations. we'll capture the deletion event in the audit log for the pilot.
05:09 Carlos: any pitfalls you've seen with redaction accuracy in other banks?
05:13 Derrick: banks often have edge cases — customer IDs embedded in attachments or paraphrased names. automated heuristics do well but you need a review loop. we'll show where the system fails and tune heuristics or add model-assisted redactors.
05:26 Priya: for our success criteria, i propose: p95 latency under 350ms for 180-token requests at nominal load, redaction precision > 98% on PII needle cases, and no persistent prompt storage for opted routes.
05:41 Maya: that sounds measurable. we'll formalize the metrics in the SOW.
05:46 Evan: who owns the workload generator and test harness?
05:49 Derrick: Redwood will provide a JMeter/locust-based harness and we can run it inside your VPC test runners or our perf cluster, depending on network isolation needs. we'll provide scripts and an excel-style benchmark sheet.
06:02 Priya: what about cost estimates for a short dedicated pilot?
06:06 Maya: i'll include two options: hosted pilot pool (lower setup time, slightly variable latency) and short-term dedicated node (higher cost, more predictable p95). I'll attach numbers in the SOW.
06:16 Janet: compliance also needs proof that the pilot will not replicate data outside region — data residency. can you run pilot in eu-west region?
06:24 Derrick: yes, we can pin to specific regions. for private deployments we can run on-prem or VPC in eu-west. for hosted, we have eu-West nodes that we can route traffic to.
06:33 Carlos: action on our side: we need to share a redaction ground truth and a sample anonymized prompt set. how much pseudonymization is acceptable?
06:42 Janet: legal wants minimal exposure; we can pseudonymize but need to keep realistic token lengths. we'll provide a masked dataset where identifiers are replaced with consistent tokens.
06:52 Maya: perfect. We'll need that by Monday to hit your three-week timeline.
06:57 Priya: Monday is tight but we can try.
07:00 Derrick: one more thing — do you have an existing DLP pipeline? we can integrate with it or run in parallel.
07:06 Priya: we have a DLP scanner that runs post-ingest. we may want Redwood to run redaction pre-ingest as an extra layer.
07:12 Derrick: noted. we'll include architecture options in the SOW: client-side redaction, proxy redaction in VPC, or Redwood-managed post-redaction hooks.
07:22 Evan: on deliverables, can you export a CSV with sample false negatives for the redaction run? that's helpful for compliance remediation.
07:29 Derrick: yes, that's part of the functional report.
07:32 Maya: quick recap: Redwood to send SOW with two hosting options, benchmark plan, timeline to run perf and redaction tests, and security annex showing KMS/SOC2/SSO. LumenBank to share redaction ground truth and sample prompts, plus region requirement.
07:47 Priya: agreed.
07:50 Janet: one more question — does Redwood store KV cache between requests for multi-turn? could that leak history?
07:58 Derrick: KV cache is in-memory per model instance and not persisted to long-term storage; if you set retention to zero and safe-mode, there won't be persisted history. we'll document cache lifecycle in the SOW.
08:12 Maya: great. i'll follow up with a summary email and SOW draft. thanks all.
08:18 Evan: thanks, bye.
08:20 [call ends — approximate timestamps are rough - transcription may include errors, some speaker attributions automated]
